rows.speaker: قراء مكة والكوفة وفقهاؤهما وابن المبارك والشافعي
rows.claim: They count the basmala as part of al-Fātiḥa and every sura.
rows.anchor: من الفاتحة، ومن كل سورة، وعليه قراء مكة والكوفة وفقهاؤهما وابن المبارك

rows.speaker: قراء المدينة والبصرة والشام ومالك والأوزاعي
rows.claim: They disagree that the basmala is part of every sura.
rows.anchor: وخالفهم قراء المدينة والبصرة والشام وفقهاؤها ومالك والأوزاعي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa stated no position here, so al-Bayḍāwī infers he did not regard it as part of the sura; Muḥammad al-Ḥasan says all text between the covers is God's speech.
rows.anchor: ولم ينص أبو حنيفة رحمه الله تعالى فيه بشيء فظن أنها ليست من السورة عنده

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: The Prophet reportedly called the basmala the first of al-Fātiḥa's seven verses.
rows.anchor: ما روى أبو هريرة رضي الله تعالى عنه، أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام قال

rows.speaker: أم سلمة
rows.claim: Umm Salama reports that the Prophet counted the basmala as a verse when reciting al-Fātiḥa.
rows.anchor: وقول أم سلمة رضي الله عنها «قرأ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم الفاتحة وعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disagreement concerns whether the basmala is an independent verse or counted with what follows; Muslims agree it is Qur'an and is written in the codices, which were carefully kept free of additions such as آمين.
rows.anchor: والإجماع على أن ما بين الدفتين كلام الله سبحانه وتعالى، والوفاق على إثباتها في المصاحف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prefixed ب is attached to an omitted verb meaning “I read,” since what follows is read; each actor supplies the verb suited to what the naming begins.
rows.anchor: والباء متعلقة بمحذوف تقديره: بسم الله أقرأ لأن الذي يتلوه مقروء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “I begin” is less suitable because nothing in the wording matches or indicates it, while “my beginning” requires an extra ellipsis.
rows.anchor: وذلك أولى من أن يضمر أبدأ لعدم ما يطابقه ويدل عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Putting the governed phrase first gives emphasis, exclusivity, and reverence; the name precedes recitation and makes an act religiously complete, as in the cited verses.
rows.anchor: وتقديم المعمول ههنا أوقع كما في قوله

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report says that any significant matter begun without the basmala is cut off or incomplete.
rows.anchor: كل أمر ذي بال لا يبدأ فيه ببسم الله فهو أبتر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative takes ب as accompaniment: read while seeking blessing through God's name.
rows.anchor: وقيل الباء للمصاحبة، والمعنى متبركا باسم الله تعالى اقرأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basmala and following words through the sura are placed on the servants' tongues to teach invocation, praise, and asking for grace.
rows.anchor: وهذه وما بعده إلى آخر السورة مقول على ألسنة العباد ليعلموا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bāʾ is kasra because these particles are obligatorily prepositional, like the kasra of the imperative lām and the genitive lām before nouns.
rows.anchor: وإنما كسرت ومن حق الحروف المفردة أن تفتح، لاختصاصها باللزوم الحرفية والجر

rows.speaker: أصحابنا البصريين
rows.claim: The Basrans derive اسم from a shortened form whose ending was dropped through frequent use; its beginning was made still and hamzat al-waṣl added to start it with a vowel.
rows.anchor: والاسم عند أصحابنا البصريين من الأسماء التي حذفت أعجازها لكثرة الاستعمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Bayḍāwī calls the metathesis proposal remote and irregular, and derives اسم from elevation because it raises the named thing and marks it.
rows.anchor: والقلب بعيد غير مطرد، واشتقاقه من السمو لأنه رفعة للمسمى

rows.speaker: الكوفيون
rows.claim: The Kufans derive اسم from السمة, originally وسم, with initial wāw deleted and hamzat al-waṣl compensating for it.
rows.anchor: وقيل أصله لاه مصدر لاه يليه ليها ولاها، إذا احتجب وارتفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects the Kufan etymology because Arabic does not use an initial hamza this way after deleting a word's first letter.
rows.anchor: ورد بأن الهمزة لم تعهد داخلة على ما حذف صدره في كلامهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shortened forms سم and سم occur, as a poetic line attests.
rows.anchor: ومن لغاته سم وسم قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If اسم means the spoken expression, it differs from its referent: sounds are discontinuous and vary across peoples and times, whereas the thing named does not.
rows.anchor: والاسم إن أريد به اللفظ فغير المسمى، لأنه يتألف من أصوات متقطعة غير قارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If اسم means the entity itself, it is the referent, but that usage is not well established.
rows.anchor: وإن أريد به ذات الشيء فهو المسمى لكنه لم يشتهر بهذا المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the commands to bless and glorify God's name, اسم can mean the spoken name, whose wording must be kept free of obscenity and discourtesy just as God and His attributes are free of defects.
rows.anchor: المراد به اللفظ لأنه كما يجب تنزيه ذاته سبحانه وتعالى وصفاته عن النقائص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another analysis treats اسم as pleonastic, as in the cited poetic expression.
rows.anchor: أو الاسم فيه مقحم كما في قول الشاعر

rows.speaker: الشيخ أبو الحسن الأشعري
rows.claim: Al-Ashʿarī treats the name as an attribute and divides attributes into what is identical with the named essence, other than it, or neither it nor other than it.
rows.anchor: وإن أريد به الصفة، كما هو رأي الشيخ أبي الحسن الأشعري، انقسم انقسام الصفة عنده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The formula says “in the name of God” rather than “by God” because blessing and seeking help are through remembrance of His name, or to distinguish oath-taking from seeking blessing.
rows.anchor: وإنما قال بسم الله ولم يقل بالله، لأن التبرك والاستعانة بذكر اسمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The written alif is omitted from بسم through frequent use, with the bāʾ lengthened in its place.
rows.anchor: ولم تكتب الألف على ما هو وضع الخط لكثرة الاستعمال وطولت الباء عوضا عنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الله derives from إله by deleting the hamza and compensating with alif-lām; it is now exclusive to the true deity, though إله originally named any object of worship.
rows.anchor: والله أصله إله، فحذفت الهمزة وعوض عنها الألف واللام ولذلك قيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One etymology derives إله from worship; further proposals connect it with bewilderment, finding rest in God, seeking refuge in fear, or a young animal's attachment to its mother.
rows.anchor: واشتقاقه من أله ألهة وألوهة وألوهية بمعنى عبد، ومنه تأله واستأله، وقيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A proposal derives it from وله, “to be bewildered,” with original wāw changing to hamza; the plural آلهة rather than أولهة argues against it.
rows.anchor: وكان أصله ولاه فقلبت الواو همزة لاستثقال الكسرة عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited poem attests the use of لاه as God's name among tribal elders.
rows.anchor:
كحلفة من أبي رباح
يشهدها لاهه الكبار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some regard الله as the proper name of God's unique essence because it alone accepts His attributes and cannot imply a partner in the confession of divine unity.
rows.anchor: وقيل علم لذاته المخصوصة لأنه يوصف ولا يوصف به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stronger view is that الله was originally descriptive, as derivation and the sense of “God in the heavens” indicate, but exclusive usage made it function like a proper name.
rows.anchor: والأظهر أنه وصف في أصله لكنه لما غلب عليه بحيث لا يستعمل في غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another proposal takes the word from Syriac لاه, adapted by dropping its final alif and adding lām.
rows.anchor: وقيل أصله لاها بالسريانية فعرب بحذف الألف الأخيرة، وإدخال اللام عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's lām is emphatic when preceded by fatḥa or ḍamma; omitting the alif in pronunciation is an error that invalidates prayer and does not form an explicit oath, though poetry may force it.
rows.anchor: وتفخيم لامه إذا انفتح ما قبله أو انضم سنة، وقيل مطلقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الرحمن and الرحيم are intensive forms of mercy; human mercy is tenderness, but divine names refer to the resulting beneficence rather than an emotional state.
rows.anchor: اسمان بنيا للمبالغة من رحم، كالغضبان من غضب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الرحمن is stronger than الرحيم because the added form indicates added meaning; this difference can concern quantity or quality.
rows.anchor: لأن زيادة البناء تدل على زيادة المعنى كما في قطع وقطع وكبار وكبار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On a quantitative reading, God is “Merciful of this world” to believers and unbelievers alike, and “Compassionate in the next” specifically to believers.
rows.anchor: يا رحمن الدنيا لأنه يعم المؤمن والكافر، ورحيم الآخرة لأنه يخص المؤمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On a qualitative reading, الرحمن covers both worlds while الرحيم covers this world, since all afterlife blessings are immense but worldly blessings range from great to small.
rows.anchor: لأن النعم الأخروية كلها جسام، وأما النعم الدنيوية فجليلة وحقيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although one might expect the less to precede the greater, الرحمن comes first because worldly mercy precedes the afterlife and because the name has become exclusive to God.
rows.anchor: وإنما قدم والقياس يقتضي الترقي من الأدنى إلى الأعلى، لتقدم رحمة الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الرحمن points to the great blessings; الرحيم then includes the blessings left out and may also preserve the verse endings.
rows.anchor: أو لأن الرحمن لما دل على جلائل النعم وأوصلها ذكر الرحيم ليتناول ما خرج منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Bayḍāwī's stronger grammatical view is that الرحمن is indeclinable, despite its exclusive association with God and the usual feminine patterns of its class.
rows.anchor: والأظهر أنه غير مصروف وإن حظر اختصاصه بالله تعالى أن يكون له مؤنث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These particular names teach that only the true God deserves to be invoked for every need: He owns all blessings, immediate and future, great and small, and alone enables their delivery and use.
rows.anchor: وإنما خص التسمية بهذه الأسماء ليعلم العارف أن المستحق لأن يستعان به في مجامع الأمور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥamd is praise for chosen excellence, including a blessing, while madḥ is praise for any excellence; one praises knowledge but merely commends beauty.
rows.anchor: هو الثناء على الجميل الاختياري من نعمة أو غيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some regard ḥamd and madḥ as equivalent; shukr is gratitude for a blessing expressed in speech, action, and belief.
rows.anchor: والشكر: مقابلة النعمة قولا وعملا واعتقادا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gratitude is broader than praise and commendation in one respect but narrower in another; praise is its chief expression because it displays blessings and makes gratitude audible.
rows.anchor: فهو أعم منهما من وجه، وأخص من آخر ولما كان الحمد من شعب الشكر

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report calls praise the head of gratitude and says one who does not praise God has not thanked Him.
rows.anchor: الحمد رأس الشكر، وما شكر الله من لم يحمده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word is nominative as a subject with لله as predicate, though an accusative reading exists; nominative signals praise as universal and enduring rather than newly arising.
rows.anchor: وإنما عدل عنه إلى الرفع ليدل على عموم الحمد وثباته له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite article can mark the genus or all praise: in reality every good comes from God, directly or through an intermediary, as 16:53 says.
rows.anchor: إذ الحمد في الحقيقة كله له، إذ ما من خير إلا وهو موليه بوسط أو بغير وسط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The entitlement to praise implies that God is living, powerful, willing, and knowing.
rows.anchor: وفيه إشعار بأنه تعالى حي قادر مريد عالم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Two recitations assimilate the dāl and lām in either direction, treating them as one word because the terms are used together.
rows.anchor: وقرىء الحمد لله بإتباع الدال اللام وبالعكس تنزيلا لهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rabb originally means gradual nurturing toward completion, then became an intensive description; another derivation treats it as a noun for the owner who preserves and develops what he owns.
rows.anchor: وهي تبليغ الشيء إلى كماله شيئا فشيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rabb is used of others only in a qualified phrase, whereas al-ʿālam names what makes something known and came to mean everything besides God.
rows.anchor: ولا يطلق على غيره تعالى إلا مقيدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The worlds comprise all substances and accidents, whose possibility and need for a necessary cause show God's existence; the plural gathers different genera, with rational beings predominant in its form.
rows.anchor: وهو كل ما سواه من الجواهر والأعراض، فإنها لإمكانها وافتقارها إلى مؤثر واجب لذاته تدل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative restricts the term to knowledgeable beings—angels, humans, and jinn—with other creatures included only secondarily.
rows.anchor: اسم وضع لذوي العلم من الملائكة والثقلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view means human beings here: each person contains counterparts of the greater world's substances and accidents, through which the Creator is known, as 51:21 invites people to observe themselves.
rows.anchor: عني به الناس ههنا فإن كل واحد منهم عالم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An accusative reading treats رب العالمين as praise, direct address, or an implied action indicated by الحمد.
rows.anchor: وقرىء { رب العلمين } بالنصب على المدح.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Possible things need God not only to originate them but also to keep them in existence.
rows.anchor: وفيه دليل على أن الممكنات كما هي مفتقرة إلى المحدث حال حدوثها فهي مفتقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repetition of الرحمن الرحيم supplies a causal explanation, which the commentary will explain later.
rows.anchor: كرره للتعليل على ما سنذكره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿĀṣim, al-Kisāʾī, and Yaʿqūb read mālik (“owner”); 82:19 supports God's sole command on that Day.
rows.anchor: قراءة عاصم والكسائي ويعقوب ويعضده قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The other reading, malik (“king”), is preferred for being the reading of the two sanctuaries and for its support in 40:16 and its greater majesty.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الباقون: { ملك }. وهو المختار لأنه قراءة أهل الحرمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mālik is one who disposes of owned things as he wills; malik governs subjects through command and prohibition.
rows.anchor: والمالك هو المتصرف في الأعيان المملوكة كيف يشاء من الملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other vocalizations include shortened forms and accusative or nominative forms, either as praise, circumstantial accusative, or a predicate of an omitted subject.
rows.anchor: ومالكا بالنصب على المدح أو الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Day of Judgment is the day of requital, as the proverb says, “as you do, so shall you be done by.”
rows.anchor: ويوم الدين يوم الجزاء ومنه «كما تدين تدان»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A poetic line allows the active participle to be annexed to a temporal adverb as though to an object, meaning that He owns affairs on that Day.
rows.anchor: أضاف اسم الفاعل إلى الظرف إجراء له مجرى المفعول به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-dīn is also glossed as the revealed law or obedience; the meaning is the day of requiting that religion.
rows.anchor: الطاعة. والمعنى يوم جزاء الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Day is singled out because of its greatness or because God's command alone then takes effect; the four divine descriptions establish that He alone truly deserves praise and worship.
rows.anchor: وتخصيص اليوم بالإضافة: إما لتعظيمه، أو لتفرده تعالى بنفوذ الأمر فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creation and nurture explain praise; mercy shows voluntary favor rather than an obligation imposed by prior deeds; exclusive sovereignty promises the grateful and warns the heedless.
rows.anchor: فالوصف الأول لبيان ما هو الموجب للحمد، وهو الإيجاد والتربية.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After identifying the one worthy of praise, the discourse turns from absence to direct address and from reasoning to witnessing: the servants reserve worship and seeking aid for Him.
rows.anchor: يا من هذا شأنه نخصك بالعبادة والاستعانة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shift of person is an Arabic device that refreshes speech and engages listeners, as in 10:22 and 35:9 and the cited poetry of Imruʾ al-Qays.
rows.anchor: ومن عادة العرب التفنن في الكلام والعدول من أسلوب إلى آخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إيا is the accusative pronoun stem and the attached letters distinguish speaker, addressee, and absent person; the attached forms have no grammatical case of their own.
rows.anchor: وإيا ضمير منصوب من فصل، وما يلحقه من الياء والكاف والهاء حروف زيدت

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalīl considered the following suffix to be annexed to إيا, citing a colloquial example; al-Bayḍāwī says this evidence is anomalous and unreliable.
rows.anchor: وقال الخليل: إيا مضاف إليها، واحتج بما حكاه عن بعض العرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other grammatical analyses treat إيا as the pronoun with an added support element, or treat the entire form as the pronoun.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هي الضمائر، وإيا عمدة فإنها لما فصلت عن العوامل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Readings include opening إيا's hamza and replacing it with hāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرىء { إياك } بفتح الهمزة و «هياك» بقلبها هاء.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿIbāda is the utmost submission and abasement, and is used only for submission to God.
rows.anchor: والعبادة: أقصى غاية الخضوع والتذلل ومنه طريق معبد أي مذلل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Necessary aid makes action possible; nonessential aid makes it easier or encourages it, but is not required for moral responsibility.
rows.anchor: طلب المعونة وهي: إما ضرورية، أو غير ضرورية والضرورية ما لا يتأتى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The request may seek help in all important matters or specifically in performing acts of worship; the pronoun can include the reciter, angels present, congregants, or all monotheists.
rows.anchor: المراد طلب المعونة في المهمات كلها، أو في أداء العبادات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speaker includes himself among worshippers to seek acceptance and response through their blessing, which helps explain the institution of congregational prayer.
rows.anchor: أدرج عبادته في تضاعيف عبادتهم وخلط حاجته بحاجتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fronting إياك conveys honor, concern, and exclusivity; Ibn ʿAbbās glosses it “we worship You and worship no other.”
rows.anchor: ولذلك قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما (معناه نعبدك ولا نعبد غيرك)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The worshipper should attend first to the worshipped and regard worship as a noble relation to God, not as a self-congratulatory act.
rows.anchor: والتنبيه على أن العابد ينبغي أن يكون نظره إلى المعبود أولا وبالذات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's statement “God is with us” is superior to Moses' “my Lord is with me” because the former loses sight of self in divine presence.
rows.anchor: ولذلك فضل ما حكى الله عن حبيبه حين قال:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating إياك explicitly reserves seeking help for God, while placing worship first preserves rhyme and teaches that presenting a means before one's request aids its acceptance.
rows.anchor: وكرر الضمير للتنصيص على أنه المستعان به لا غير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saying “we worship” might sound boastful, so “we seek Your help” clarifies that worship itself depends on God's aid and enabling.
rows.anchor: فعقبه بقوله: { وإياك نستعين } ليدل على أن العبادة أيضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conjunction may instead express circumstance: “we worship You while seeking Your help.”
rows.anchor: وقيل: الواو للحال والمعنى نعبدك مستعينين بك.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The imperfect verbs with kasra are a Tamīm dialect feature when the following consonant is not uḍamma.
rows.anchor: وقرىء بكسر النون فيهما وهي لغة بني تميم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Guide us” specifies the requested aid or names its chief purpose; guidance is gentle direction and is normally for good, while its use for the path to Hell in 37:23 is ironic.
rows.anchor: بيان للمعونة المطلوبة فكأنه قال: كيف أعينكم فقالوا { اهدنا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Divine guidance has four ordered kinds: faculties for recognizing interests, distinguishing signs, messengers and revealed books, and disclosure of realities by revelation, inspiration, or true dreams.
rows.anchor: ولكنها تنحصر في أجناس مترتبة:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Scripture illustrates guidance by signs at 2:10, 41:17, 21:73, 17:9, 6:90, and 29:69; the last kind is reserved for prophets and saints.
rows.anchor: وهذا قسم يختص بنيله الأنبياء والأولياء وإياه عنى بقوله:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The request seeks an increase in guidance already granted, steadfastness in it, or the further ranks that follow it; the spiritually realized ask to travel toward God and shed bodily veils.
rows.anchor: فالمطلوب إما زيادة ما منحوه من الهدى، أو الثبات عليه، أو حصول المراتب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Command and supplication share wording and meaning but differ through the speaker's elevated or lower rank, or simply through rank.
rows.anchor: والأمر والدعاء يتشاركان لفظا ومعنى ويتفاوتان بالاستعلاء والتسفل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣirāṭ derives from swallowing because the road seems to swallow its travelers; ṣaraṭ with ṣād assimilates the sīn to emphatic ṭāʾ, sometimes retaining a z-like sound.
rows.anchor: من سرط الطعام إذا ابتلعه فكأنه يسرط السابلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qunbul's Ibn Kathīr and Ruways's Yaʿqūb read the original sīn; Ḥamza uses an imāla-like z sound, and the rest read ṣād, the Qurashī form preserved in the codex.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير برواية قنبل عنه، ورويس عن يعقوب بالأصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣirāṭ is masculine or feminine like ṭarīq, and its plural is suruṭ.
rows.anchor: والثابت في الإمام وجمعه سرط ككتب وهو كالطريق في التذكير والتأنيث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The straight path is the level path of truth, identified by some as Islam; “the path of those You favored” is an emphatic explanatory apposition.
rows.anchor: المستوي والمراد به طريق الحق، وقيل: هو ملة الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apposition identifies the believers' path as straight in the strongest way, making its soundness appear self-evident.
rows.anchor: وفائدته التوكيد والتنصيص على أن طريق المسلمين هو المشهود عليه بالاستقامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The favored are variously identified as prophets; the Prophet and his Companions; or the uncorrupted, un-abrogated followers of Moses and Jesus.
rows.anchor: وقيل: { الذين أنعمت عليهم } الأنبياء، وقيل: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وأصحابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Divine favors fall into worldly and afterlife kinds; worldly favors are bestowed or acquired, with spiritual and bodily branches, while acquired favors include virtue, good character, adornment, status, and wealth.
rows.anchor: ونعم الله وإن كانت لا تحصى كما قال:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The intended favor is the final afterlife good and whatever leads to it, including forgiveness, divine approval, and residence in the highest ranks; other favors are shared with unbelievers.
rows.anchor: والمراد هو القسم الأخير وما يكون وصلة إلى نيله من الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Not those angered nor astray” may be an apposition to “those You favored,” or a qualifying description showing that true favor joins faith with safety from anger and error.
rows.anchor: بدل من { الذين } على معنى أن المنعم عليهم هم الذين سلموا من الغضب والضلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The adjective-like reading is possible if the relative is treated as indefinite or if غير becomes definite by annexation to the unique opposite group.
rows.anchor: وذلك إنما يصح بأحد تأويلين، إجراء الموصول مجرى النكرة

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr reads غير in the accusative as a circumstantial qualifier or by an implied verb, and it can also be an exception if favors include both groups.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن كثير نصبه على الحال من الضمير المجرور والعامل أنعمت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Divine anger denotes its ultimate effect, punishment; عليهم is a passive-subject phrase, unlike the earlier construction, and لا reinforces the negation in غير.
rows.anchor: والغضب: ثوران النفس إرادة الانتقام، فإذا أسند إلى الله تعالى أريد به المنتهى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A recitation adds و before الضالين, and another uses hamza in الضألين to avoid two adjacent still consonants.
rows.anchor: وقرىء { وغير الضالين } والضلال: العدول عن الطريق السوي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reported interpretation identifies those under anger as Jews and those astray as Christians, linking them to 5:60 and 5:77; the identification is also transmitted as a Prophetic report.
rows.anchor: قيل: { المغضوب عليهم } اليهود لقوله تعالى فيهم:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further interpretation calls deliberate sinners angered and those ignorant of God astray: failure of action is impiety, while failure of understanding is error.
rows.anchor: ويتجه أن يقال: المغضوب عليهم العصاة والضالين الجاهلون بالله،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The favored combine knowledge of truth with doing good; the contrasting groups each lack one of the rational or active faculties.
rows.anchor: لأن المنعم عليه من وفق للجمع بين معرفة الحق لذاته والخير للعمل به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Āmīn is an imperative noun meaning “answer/accept”; a report from Ibn ʿAbbās says the Prophet explained it as “do so.” It is built on fatḥa to avoid two adjacent still consonants.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس قال سألت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن معناه فقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Āmīn is not Qur'an, but ending the sura with it is recommended because Gabriel taught it to the Prophet as a seal on the book; ʿAlī similarly calls it the seal of the Lord of the worlds.
rows.anchor: لكن يسن ختم السورة به لقوله عليه الصلاة والسلام

rows.speaker: وائل بن حجر
rows.claim: The Prophet said آمين aloud after ولا الضالين; al-Bayḍāwī cites this for an imam's audible response in audible prayers.
rows.anchor: لما روي عن وائل بن حجر

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa is reported not to say آمين, though the better-known report says he says it quietly; a congregant says it with the imam.
rows.anchor: وعن أبي حنيفة رضي الله عنه أنه لا يقوله، والمشهور عنه أنه يخفيه

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: A Prophetic report calls al-Fātiḥa unparalleled in Torah, Gospel, and Qur'an, and identifies it as the seven oft-repeated verses and the great Qur'an.
rows.anchor: وعن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال لأبي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A visiting angel gave the Prophet two lights unavailable to earlier prophets—the opening of the Book and the end of al-Baqara—and each letter recited brings a gift.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال:

rows.speaker: حذيفة بن اليمان
rows.claim: A report says recitation of الحمد لله رب العالمين by a child among a people under destined punishment caused God to lift it from them for forty years.
rows.anchor: وعن حذيفة بن اليمان أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Glorifying God's name means guarding it against deviant interpretation and applying it to another as though the two were equal; mention الأعلى magnifies Him. One reading says سبحان ربي الأعلى.
rows.anchor: نزه اسمه عن إلحاد فيه بالتأويلات الزائغة وإطلاقه على غيره

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: When 69:52 was revealed, the Prophet instructed the companions to use its glorification in bowing; on this verse's revelation he instructed them to use it in prostration.
rows.anchor: لما نزلت { فسبح باسم ربك العظيم } قال عليه الصلاة والسلام اجعلوها في ركوعكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The companions also used supplications in bowing and prostration, saying “O God, to You I bow” and “O God, to You I prostrate.”
rows.anchor: وكانوا يقولون في الركوع اللهم لك ركعت وفي السجود اللهم لك سجدت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God created each thing and fashioned it by giving it what enables its perfection and livelihood.
rows.anchor: خلق كل شيء فسوى خلقه بأن جعل له ما به يتأتى كماله ويتم معاشه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God determined kinds, species, individuals, measures, qualities, acts, and lifespans, then directed each toward its natural or chosen acts through inclinations, inspiration, signs, and revealed verses.
rows.anchor: قدر أجناس الأشياء وأنواعها وأشخاصها ومقاديرها وصفاتها وأفعالها وآجالها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God prepares the Prophet for the easier way, whether that means preserving revelation or practicing religion, and enables him in it.
rows.anchor: ونعدك لطريقة اليسرى في حفظ الوحي، أو التدين وتوفقك لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording نيسرك rather than “make it easy for you” suits its coordination with سنقرئك and signals an intervening clause.
rows.anchor: ولهذه النكتة قال { نيسرك } لا نيسر لك عطف على { سنقرئك }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is told to remind people once his situation is established; the qualification إن نفعت الذكرى can prevent fruitless exhaustion after repeated reminders and apparent despair.
rows.anchor: بعد ما استتب لك الأمر. { إن نفعت الذكرى } لعل هذه الشرطية إنما جاءت بعد تكرير التذكير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the conditional censures the hearers by doubting that reminders affect them, or says reminding is obligatory only when benefit is expected, so the Prophet should leave those who turn away.
rows.anchor: الآية، أو لذم المذكورين واستبعاد تأثير الذكرى فيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person who fears God will take heed by considering the reminder and recognizing its truth; the phrase includes both the spiritually certain and the hesitant.
rows.anchor: سيتعظ وينتفع بها من يخشى الله تعالى بأن يتأمل فيها فيعلم حقيقتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The most wretched avoids the reminder; this means either the unbeliever, who is worse than the sinner, or the most deeply immersed of unbelievers.
rows.anchor: { الأشقى } الكافر فإنه أشقى من الفاسق، أو { الأشقى } من الكفرة

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The “greatest Fire” is Hell, since the Prophet said earthly fire is one seventieth of Hellfire; an alternative identifies it with Hell's lowest pit.
rows.anchor: ناركم هذه جزء من سبعين جزأ من نار جهنم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The damned neither die and find relief nor live a life that benefits them.
rows.anchor: فيستريح. { ولا يحيى } حياة تنفعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person who succeeds purifies himself of unbelief and sin, increases in piety, prepares for prayer, or pays the alms.
rows.anchor: تطهر من الكفر والمعصية، أو تكثر من التقوى من الزكاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembering God with heart and tongue and then praying echoes 20:14; ذكر may mean the opening takbīr instead.
rows.anchor: بقلبه ولسانه { فصلى } كقوله:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes تزكى as giving the fitr alms, remembering God as the Eid takbīr, and prayer as the Eid prayer.
rows.anchor: وقيل { تزكى } تصدق للفطر { وذكر اسم ربه } كبره يوم العيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People prefer worldly life and so neglect what would make them happy in the afterlife; the address may target the wretched, be commanded through قل, or address everyone because worldly striving generally predominates.
rows.anchor: والخطاب للأشقين على الالتفات أو على إضمار قل، أو للكل

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abū ʿAmr reads the verb in the third person plural rather than second person.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو بالياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The afterlife is better because its pleasure is intrinsic and free of harm, and it lasts without end.
rows.anchor: فإن نعيمها ملذ بالذات خالص عن الغوائل لا انقطاع له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “This” refers to the preceding promise of success, which gathers the religion's central teaching and the essence of revealed books.
rows.anchor: الإشارة إلى ما سبق من { قد أفلح } فإنه جامع أمر الديانة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reference to Abraham's and Moses' scriptures is an appositional explanation of the earlier scriptures.
rows.anchor: بدل من الصحف الأولى

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report promises ten good deeds for every letter God revealed to Abraham, Moses, and Muhammad to whoever recites this sura.
rows.anchor: من قرأ سورة الأعلى أعطاه الله عشر حسنات بعدد كل حرف أنزله الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ghāshiya is either the calamity whose terrors overwhelm people on Judgment Day or the Fire, as in 14:50.
rows.anchor: الداهية التي تغشى الناس بشدائدها يعني يوم القيامة، أو النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The faces on that Day are humbled and abased.
rows.anchor: وجوه يومئذ خشعة } ذليلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their labor is exhausting work in Hell, such as hauling chains and climbing its rises and hollows, or wasted effort in worldly deeds that will not benefit them then.
rows.anchor: تعمل ما تتعب فيه كجر السلاسل وخوضها في النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The faces enter a Fire whose heat is extreme; readings include a form meaning God causes them to enter and a doubled form for intensity.
rows.anchor: } تدخلها وقرأ أبو عمرو ويعقوب وأبو بكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are given water from a spring at the peak of its heat.
rows.anchor: بلغت أناها في الحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḍarīʿ is dried shibriq thorn, which camels graze while fresh; another view makes it a hellish tree resembling that thorn.
rows.anchor: يبيس الشبرق وهو شوك ترعاه الإبل ما دام رطبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The thorn may be one group's food while others receive zaqqūm or ghislin; alternatively their food is whatever camels avoid because it harms and does not nourish.
rows.anchor: ولعله طعام هؤلاء والزقوم والغسلين طعام غيرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The food neither nourishes nor relieves hunger, since nourishment serves one of those two purposes.
rows.anchor: والمقصود من الطعام أحد الأمرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The other faces are beautiful and radiant or enjoying comfort.
rows.anchor: ذات بهجة أو متنعمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are pleased with their striving when they see its reward.
rows.anchor: رضيت بعملها لما رأت ثوابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The garden is high in location or in rank.
rows.anchor: علية المحل أو القدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition on hearing may address the listener or the faces; readings vary between passive masculine and feminine. لغية can mean idle talk, a futile utterance, or a person who indulges in it.
rows.anchor: يا مخاطب أو الوجوه، وقرأ على بناء المفعول بالياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Paradise's people speak remembrance and wisdom, not vain talk.
rows.anchor: فإن كلام أهل الجنة الذكر والحكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The spring's water flows without stopping; its indefinite form conveys grandeur.
rows.anchor: يجري ماؤها ولا ينقطع والتنكير للتعظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The couches are elevated in height or rank.
rows.anchor: رفيعة السمك أو القدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Goblets are handleless vessels placed within reach.
rows.anchor: جمع كوب وهي آنية لا عروة لها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cushions, whose plural derives from either vocalization of نمرقة, are arranged in rows beside one another.
rows.anchor: وسائد جمع نمرقة بالفتح والضم. { مصفوفة } بعضها إلى بعض.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fine carpets are spread out throughout the garden.
rows.anchor: بسط فاخرة جمع زريبة. { مبثوثة } مبسوطة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People should look reflectively at camels: their construction shows divine power and wise care, fitting them to haul loads far away, rise under burdens, follow a driver, graze many plants, and endure long thirst.
rows.anchor: خلقا دالا على كمال قدرته وحسن تدبيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Camels are singled out because they display the signs found in animals, the most skillfully fashioned compound creatures, and are the Arabs' most astonishing example.
rows.anchor: ولذلك خصت بالذكر لبيان الآيات المنبثة في الحيوانات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative reads the camels as clouds by metaphor.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد بها السحاب على الاستعارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sky is raised without pillars.
rows.anchor: وإلى السماء كيف رفعت } بلا عمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mountains are set firmly in place and do not tilt.
rows.anchor: فهي راسخة لا تميل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth is spread until it forms a resting place; one reading makes all four creation verbs first-person active with their object pronouns omitted.
rows.anchor: بسطت حتى صارت مهادا، وقرىء الأفعال الأربعة على بناء الفاعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reflection on simple and composite creatures verifies the Creator's power and therefore resurrection; the reminder follows as a consequence.
rows.anchor: إلى أنواع المخلوقات من البسائط والمركبات ليتحققوا كمال قدرة الخالق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's responsibility is to deliver the reminder; he is not accountable if people fail to reflect or heed it.
rows.anchor: فلا عليك إن لم ينظروا ولم يذكروا إذ ما عليك إلا البلاغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is not a controller over them; al-Kisāʾī reads the sīn form and Ḥamza uses an imāla-like sound.
rows.anchor: بمتسلط، وعن الكسائي بالسين على الأصل وحمزة بالإشمام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception can instead mean “but whoever turns away and disbelieves.”
rows.anchor: لكن من تولى وكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One analysis connects the exception to the warning: fighting and killing unbelievers is a form of control, so they face worldly jihad and the greater punishment in the next life.
rows.anchor: وقيل متصل فإن جهاد الكفار وقتلهم تسلط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another analysis links the exception to “remind”: remind everyone except one who turns away persistently and thereby deserves the greatest punishment; a reading highlights the exception.
rows.anchor: وقيل هو استثناء من قوله { فذكر } أي فذكر إلا من تولى وأصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The greatest punishment is that of the afterlife.
rows.anchor: { فيعذبه الله العذاب الأكبر } يعني عذاب الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their return is to God; a strengthened reading of إياب gives a derived verbal noun, or a form from الأوب with the two wāws altered for assimilation.
rows.anchor: رجوعهم، وقرىء بالتشديد على أنه فيعلل مصدر فيعل من الإياب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will account for them at the gathering; placing the predicate first intensifies the threat and restricts judgment to Him.
rows.anchor: في المحشر، وتقديم الخبر للتخصيص والمبالغة في الوعيد

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report promises an easy reckoning to whoever recites al-Ghāshiya.
rows.anchor: من قرأ سورة الغاشية حاسبه الله حسابا يسيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iram is an explanatory apposition for ʿĀd, with an implied “tribe” or “people” if Iram is their town; it may name the earliest ʿĀd after their ancestor and is feminine proper noun.
rows.anchor: عطف بيان ل { عاد } على تقدير مضاف أي سبط { إرم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ذات العماد can mean lofty buildings, tall bodies, or elevation and firmness.
rows.anchor: ذات البناء الرفيع أو القدود الطوال، أو الرفعة والثبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A story says ʿĀd's Shaddād inherited the kingdom, built a paradise-like garden called Iram in the deserts of ʿAdan, then died with his household when a heavenly cry struck as he approached; ʿAbd Allāh ibn Qilāba reportedly stumbled upon it while seeking camels.
rows.anchor: فسمع بذكر الجنة فبنى على مثالها في بعض صحاري عدن جنة وسماها إرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause “the like of which was not created in the lands” further describes Iram whether it is understood as a tribe or a town.
rows.anchor: صفة أخرى ل { إرم } والضمير لها سواء جعلت { إرم } القبيلة أو البلدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thamūd cut rock and made homes in it, as 26:149 says they carved houses from mountains; the valley is Wādī al-Qurā.
rows.anchor: قطعوه واتخذوه منازل لقوله: { وتنحتون من الجبال بيوتا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh is called “possessor of stakes” either because of his many soldiers and their tents or because he tortured people with stakes.
rows.anchor: لكثرة جنوده ومضاربهم التي كانوا يضربونها إذا نزلوا، أو لتعذيبه بالأوتاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who transgressed can syntactically qualify ʿĀd, Thamūd, and Pharaoh, or can be a separate expression of blame in either case ending.
rows.anchor: صفة للمذكورين «عاد» { وثمود } { وفرعون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their corruption consisted of unbelief and injustice.
rows.anchor: بالكفر والظلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God poured mixed forms of punishment on them; the word whip evokes strands twisted together, and the worldly scourge is slight beside the afterlife's sword-like punishment.
rows.anchor: ما خلط لهم من أنواع العذاب، وأصله الخلط وإنما سمي به الجلد المضفور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God lies in wait like an observer at an ambush, a figure for keeping punishment ready for sinners.
rows.anchor: وهو تمثيل لإرصاده العصاة بالعقاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These verses connect to the Lord's watch over the afterlife: people attend only to worldly pleasures although God tests them through both wealth and restricted provision.
rows.anchor: متصل بقوله: { إن ربك لبالمرصاد } كأنه قيل إنه { لبالمرصاد } من الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person mistakes wealth, status, and ease for proof that God has honored him; the syntax makes the statement the predicate after an intervening conditional circumstance.
rows.anchor: اختبره بالغنى واليسر. { فأكرمه ونعمه } بالجاه والمال. { فيقول ربى أكرمن } فضلني بما أعطاني، وهو خبر المبتدأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When tested with poverty and constricted provision, a person wrongly concludes that God has humiliated him; restriction may instead bring honor in both worlds, whereas ease can lead to enemies or worldly obsession.
rows.anchor: فإن التقتير قد يؤدي إلى كرامة الدارين، والتوسعة قد تفضي إلى قصد الأعداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كلا rebukes the person's inference: expansion is generosity, and withholding it is not humiliation; some readers omit the final yāʾ of أكرمن and أهانن, and Ibn ʿĀmir reads قدر with doubled dāl.
rows.anchor: لأن التوسعة تفضل والإخلال به لا يكون إهانة، وقرأ ابن عامر والكوفيون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their actual conduct is worse than their mistaken words: they fail to spend compassionately on orphans and do not even urge their families to feed the poor; Kufans read تحاضون.
rows.anchor: بل فعلهم أسوأ من قولهم وأدل على تهالكهم بالمال وهو أنهم لا يكرمون اليتيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They consume inheritance greedily, including shares of women and children whom they excluded, or knowingly consume what the deceased had accumulated from lawful and unlawful sources.
rows.anchor: فإنهم كانوا لا يورثون النساء والصبيان ويأكلون أنصباءهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: التراث is inheritance, with an original wāw; لما means that unlike food is lumped together in consumption.
rows.anchor: الميراث وأصله وراث. { أكلا لما }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Returning to the Lord means returning to His command or to the appointed death/resurrection; the latter wording supports the view that souls existed in a holy realm before bodies.
rows.anchor: إلى أمره أو موعده بالموت، ويشعر ذلك بقول من قال:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The soul is pleased with what it receives and is approved by God.
rows.anchor: بما أوتيت. { مرضية } عند الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Entering among God's servants means joining the righteous, or joining the near ones whose reciprocal illumination is like facing mirrors; it may also mean re-entering the bodies left behind.
rows.anchor: في جملة عبادي الصالحين. { وادخلي جنتي } معهم أو في زمرة المقربين فتستضيء بنورهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Entering God's Garden is entry into the reward prepared for the soul.
rows.anchor: وادخلي دار ثوابي التي أعدت لك

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report promises forgiveness for reciting al-Fajr during the ten nights and a light on the Resurrection Day for reciting it at other times.
rows.anchor: من قرأ سورة الفجر في الليالي العشر غفر له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The boast of having squandered abundant wealth refers to spending for show and rivalry, or in hostility toward the Messenger.
rows.anchor: كثيرا، من تلبد الشيء إذا اجتمع، والمراد ما أنفقه سمعة ومفاخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The boaster thinks no one saw his expenditure or will ask him about it, but God sees it and will judge it.
rows.anchor: حين كان ينفق أو بعد ذلك فيسأله عنه، يعني أن الله سبحانه وتعالى يراه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gave him two eyes with which to see.
rows.anchor: ألم نجعل له عينين } يبصر بهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tongue expresses inner thought; the lips cover the mouth and assist speech, eating, and drinking.
rows.anchor: يترجم به عن ضميره. { وشفتين } يستر بهما فاه ويستعين بهما على النطق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ما in the oaths means “the one who built/spread them,” emphasizing the agent's description; their construction shows His existence and perfect power.
rows.anchor: ومن بناها وإنما أوثرت على من لإرادة معنى الوصفية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Making the particles source nouns would remove the agents and disrupt the grammatical sequence continued by “inspired it,” unless God is supplied implicitly.
rows.anchor: وجعل الماءات مصدرية يجرد الفعل عن الفاعل ويخل بنظم قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite soul may generalize across souls, as at 81:14, or magnify and refer specifically to Adam.
rows.anchor: وتنكير { نفس } للتكثير كما في قوله تعالى:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inspiring the soul to recognize its sin and piety means explaining and defining both states or enabling it to perform them.
rows.anchor: وإلهام الفجور والتقوى إفهامهما وتعريف حالهما أو التمكين من الإتيان بهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The success clause answers the oath; its lām is omitted for length. The oaths exhort people to perfect the soul through knowledge of the Creator and gratitude for His favors.
rows.anchor: أنماها بالعلم والعمل جواب القسم، وحذف اللام للطول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the oath passage digresses on the soul and its answer is omitted: God would destroy Mecca's unbelievers as He destroyed Thamūd for rejecting Ṣāliḥ.
rows.anchor: وقيل هو استطراد بذكر بعض أحوال النفس، والجواب محذوف تقديره ليدمدمن الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The loser diminishes and conceals the soul through ignorance and disobedience; the form دسّى contracts from دسس, like تقضى from تقضض.
rows.anchor: نقصها وأخفاها بالجهالة والفسوق، وأصل دسى دسس كتقضي وتقضض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thamūd denied because of its tyranny, or because it rejected the promised punishment described by طغوى; the form derives from طغياها, with a spelling distinction between noun and adjective.
rows.anchor: بسبب طغيانها، أو بما أوعدت به من عذابها ذي الطغوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إذ انبعث can be a time clause for the denial or for tyranny; “their most wretched one” is Qudār ibn Sālif or him together with his accomplices.
rows.anchor: حين قام ظرف ل { كذبت } أو طغوى. { أشقها } أشقى ثمود وهو قدار بن سالف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The superlative can refer to one or many because the people shared responsibility in allowing the camel's slaughter.
rows.anchor: أو هو ومن مالأه على قتل الناقة فإن أفعل التفضيل إذا أضفته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's messenger warns Thamūd to leave God's camel alone and not prevent its allotted drink.
rows.anchor: أي ذروا ناقة الله واحذروا عقرها. { وسقيها } وسقيها فلا تذودوها عنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They rejected the warning, hamstrung her, and God overwhelmed them with punishment for their sin; دمدم evokes layering the people with punishment.
rows.anchor: فأطبق عليهم العذاب وهو من تكرير قولهم ناقة مدمومة إذا ألبسها الشحم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made the punishment uniform so no young or old escaped, or annihilated all Thamūd.
rows.anchor: فسوى الدمدمة بينهم أو عليهم فلم يفلت منهم صغير ولا كبير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final clause can mean God feared no consequence of the punishment or destruction of Thamūd; wāw is circumstantial, while Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read fa-lā as a connective.
rows.anchor: أي عاقبة الدمدمة أو عاقبة هلاك ثمود وتبعتها فيبقي بعض الإبقاء

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report says reciting al-Shams is like giving charity over everything illuminated by the sun and moon.
rows.anchor: من قرأ سورة والشمس فكأنما تصدق بكل شيء طلعت عليه الشمس والقمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception may be disconnected, or connected to an omitted clause meaning that he gives only to seek God's countenance, not to repay a favor.
rows.anchor: استثناء منقطع أو متصل عن محذوف مثل لا يؤتى إلا ابتغاء وجه ربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God promises reward that will satisfy the recipient.
rows.anchor: وعد بالثواب الذي يرضيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These verses were revealed concerning Abū Bakr, who bought and freed Bilāl and other people persecuted by polytheists; the wretched person is consequently identified as Abū Jahl or Umayya ibn Khalaf.
rows.anchor: والآيات نزلت في أبي بكر رضي الله تعالى عنه حين اشترى بلالا في جماعة

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report promises enough provision to satisfy the reciter and relief from hardship with an easy path.
rows.anchor: من قرأ سورة والليل أعطاه الله سبحانه وتعالى حتى يرضى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The afterlife is enduring and free of worldly defects, whereas this life passes and is mixed with harms; the Prophet's final state will exceed his beginning.
rows.anchor: فإنها باقية خالصة عن الشوائب وهذه فانية مشوبة بالمضار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After promising continuing revelation and honor in this life, God promises the Prophet an even greater afterlife gift, including perfection, triumph, and elevation of the religion.
rows.anchor: وعد له ما هو أعلى وأجل من ذلك في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise embraces what God gave him and what was stored for him beyond comprehension; the lām is emphatic, not an oath, and its conjunction with سوف guarantees delayed fulfillment.
rows.anchor: وجمعها مع سوف للدلالة على أن الإعطاء كائن لا محالة وإن تأخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reminding the Prophet of past care assures him that God will continue to care for him despite any delay; يجد means “know” or “find,” with يتيم analyzed as second object or circumstantial predicate.
rows.anchor: تعديد لما أنعم عليه تنبيها على أنه كما أحسن إليه فيما مضى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ضالا means lacking knowledge of rulings; God then taught him by revelation, inspiration, and enabling sound reflection.
rows.anchor: عن علم الحكم والأحكام. { فهدى } فعلمك بالوحي والإلهام والتوفيق للنظر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternative reports say the Prophet lost his way while Abū Ṭālib took him to Syria or while Ḥalīma brought him after weaning; God guided him away from uncle or grandfather.
rows.anchor: وقيل وجدك ضالا في الطريق حين خرج بك أبو طالب إلى الشام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God found the Prophet poor with dependents and enriched him through the profits of trade.
rows.anchor: فقيرا ذا عيال. { فأغنى } بما حصل لك من ربح التجارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not overpower an orphan to seize his property; a reading says not to frown at him.
rows.anchor: فلا تغلبه على ماله لضعفه، وقرىء فلا تكهر أي فلا تعبس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not rebuke or drive away a petitioner.
rows.anchor: فلا تزجره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Speaking of the Lord's blessing is gratitude; another interpretation makes the blessing prophethood and the command an order to proclaim it.
rows.anchor: فإن التحدث بها شكرها. وقيل المراد بالنعمة النبوة والتحديث بها تبليغها

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report promises acceptance among those for whom Muhammad may intercede and deeds equal to the number of orphans and petitioners for reciting al-Ḍuḥā.
rows.anchor: من قرأ سورة والضحى جعله الله سبحانه وتعالى فيمن يرضى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Opening the Prophet's breast means expanding it for communion with God and addressing people, filling it with wisdom and removing ignorance, or making revelation easier to receive.
rows.anchor: ألم نفسحه حتى وسع مناجاة الحق ودعوة الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A transmitted account says Gabriel opened the Prophet's chest in childhood or on the day of the covenant, washed his heart, and filled it with faith and knowledge; al-Bayḍāwī relates it to the preceding sense.
rows.anchor: أن جبريل عليه الصلاة والسلام أتى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في صباه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rhetorical question emphatically denies that his breast was not expanded, thereby affirming the expansion.
rows.anchor: ومعنى الاستفهام إنكار نفي الانشراح مبالغة في إثباته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The burden lifted from the Prophet is a heavy load.
rows.anchor: ووضعنا عنك وزرك } عبأك الثقيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That burden may be pre-mission lapses, ignorance of rulings, bewilderment, the difficulty of receiving revelation, grief at his people's error, or their persistence and abuse when he called them to faith.
rows.anchor: من ثقل الحمل وهو ما ثقل عليه من فرطاته قبل البعثة، أو جهله بالحكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When finished with conveying the message, the Prophet should exert himself in worship to thank God for past blessings and promised future blessings; alternatively he should worship after warfare or pray then supplicate.
rows.anchor: من التبيلغ. { فانصب } فاتعب في العبادة شكرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet should direct his hope and requests to God alone, who alone can help him.
rows.anchor: بالسؤال ولا تسأل غيره فإنه القادر وحده على إسعافك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading in the passive sense means “make people desire” God's reward.
rows.anchor: وقرىء «فرغب» أي فرغب الناس إلى طلب ثوابه

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report likens reciting this sura to visiting the Prophet while distressed and relieving him.
rows.anchor: من قرأ سورة ألم نشرح فكأنما جاءني وأنا مغتم ففرج عني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The One who created and reduced humanity is the wisest in making and governing; therefore He can restore people and requite them, as argued elsewhere.
rows.anchor: والمعنى أليس الذي فعل ذلك من الخلق والرد { بأحكم الحكمين } صنعا وتدبيرا

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report promises health and certainty in life and reward after death proportionate to the number of reciters of al-Tīn.
rows.anchor: من قرأ سورة والتين أعطاه الله العافية واليقين ما دام حيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command is to recite the Qur'an beginning with God's name, or to recite seeking His aid.
rows.anchor: باسمه سبحانه وتعالى. أو مستعينا به.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Who created” can describe the One who owns creation or the One who created everything; the next verse then singles out humanity as the most remarkable creation.
rows.anchor: أي الذي له الخلق أو الذي خلق كل شيء، ثم أفرد ما هو أشرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human being created from a clot is first left unspecified and then explained to magnify the creation's marvel; علق is plural by agreement with الإنسان in collective meaning.
rows.anchor: فأبهم أولا ثم فسر تفخيما لخلقه ودلالة على عجيب فطرته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since knowing God is the first obligation, the opening verses first show His existence, immense power, and complete wisdom.
rows.anchor: ولما كان أول الواجبات معرفة الله سبحانه وتعالى نزل أولا ما يدل على وجوده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second command to recite either intensifies the first, or distinguishes unrestricted recitation from proclamation or reciting in prayer; it may follow the Prophet's response “I cannot read.”
rows.anchor: تكرير للمبالغة، أو الأول مطلق والثاني للتبليغ أو في الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is more generous than every generous person because He gives without compensation and forbears without fear; He alone is truly generous.
rows.anchor: الزائد في الكرم على كل كريم فإنه سبحانه وتعالى ينعم بلا عوض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God taught writing with the pen, which preserves knowledge and conveys it to distant people; a reading explicitly adds the word “writing.”
rows.anchor: أي الخط بالقلم، وقد قرىء به لتقيد به العلوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God teaches through created faculties, established signs, and revealed verses, including teaching reading to one who could not read.
rows.anchor: بخلق القوى ونصب الدلائل وإنزال الآيات فيعلمك القراءة وإن لم تكن قارئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God recounts humanity's beginning and destination to show the favor of raising it from the lowest rank to the highest, affirm His lordship and generosity, and move from rational proof to sensory evidence.
rows.anchor: وقد عدد سبحانه وتعالى مبدأ أمر الإنسان ومنتهاه إظهارا لما أنعم عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كلا rebukes the one who rejects God's favor through transgression; a person transgresses when he sees himself as self-sufficient.
rows.anchor: كلا } ردع لمن كفر بنعمة الله بطغيانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause means that a person sees himself and regards himself as independent; استغنى is the second object of رأى, meaning “know.”
rows.anchor: أن رأى نفسه، واستغنى مفعوله الثاني لأنه بمعنى علم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The direct address warns the human being about the consequence of transgression; الرجعى is a verbal noun like البشرى.
rows.anchor: الخطاب للإنسان على الالتفات تهديدا وتحذيرا من عاقبة الطغيان، و { الرجعى } مصدر كالبشرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verses were revealed about Abū Jahl, who threatened to trample Muhammad's neck if he saw him prostrating, then retreated and described a trench of fire, terror, and wings between them.
rows.anchor: نزلت في أبي جهل قال لو رأيت محمدا ساجدا لوطئت عنقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The generic indefinite “a servant” intensifies the ugliness of forbidding prayer and magnifies the worshipper's servitude.
rows.anchor: ولفظ العبد وتنكيره للمبالغة في تقبيح النهي والدلالة على كمال عبودية المنهي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated أَرَأَيْتَ construction has the same grammatical function; its conditional is the second object, and its answer is omitted but supplied by the later condition. God sees the person's guidance and error.
rows.anchor: أرأيت تكرير للأول وكذا الذي في قوله:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading asks whether the forbidding person is himself guided and commands piety as he understands idol worship, or whether he is a denier who turns from truth; God sees all his states.
rows.anchor: إن كان ذلك الناهي على هدى فيما ينهى عنه، أو آمرا { بالتقوى }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation marvels that the worshipper is guided and commands piety while the forbidding person denies and turns away.
rows.anchor: وقيل المعنى { أرأيت الذي ينهى عبدا } يصلي والمنهي على الهدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further reading shifts the second question to the unbeliever, as if a judge addresses each of two litigants in turn.
rows.anchor: وقيل الخطاب في الثانية مع الكافر فإنه سبحانه وتعالى كالحاكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mention of commanding piety heightens the rebuke; it is omitted from the description of the prohibition because forbidding prayer suffices, or because prayer represents action and invitation comprehensively.
rows.anchor: ولعله ذكر الأمر بالتقوى في التعجب والتوبيخ ولم يتعرض له في النهي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كلا rebukes the one who forbids; if he does not stop, God will seize him by the forelock and drag him to Hell. Readings vary in the emphatic verb, whose written alif reflects pause and whose understood object is the offender's forelock.
rows.anchor: { كلا } ردع للناهي. { لئن لم ينته } عما هو فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lying, sinning forelock renames the forelock in apposition; its traits are figuratively attributed from its owner for emphasis, and it may be read in nominative or accusative.
rows.anchor: بدل من الناصية وإنما جاز لوصفها، وقرئت بالرفع على هي ناصية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The offender is told to summon the people of his council to help him; a nādī is the gathering place where people confer.
rows.anchor: أهل ناديه ليعينوه وهو المجلس الذي ينتدي فيه القوم

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report says Abū Jahl confronted the praying Prophet; after the Prophet rebuked him, Abū Jahl boasted that he had the largest council in the valley, prompting the revelation.
rows.anchor: روي أنا أبا جهل لعنه الله مر برسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو يصلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The zabāniya drag the offender to Hell; the term's singular may be zabniya, from pushing away, or a nisba form whose tāʾ replaces yāʾ.
rows.anchor: ليجروه إلى النار وهو في الأصل الشرط واحدها زبنية كعفرية من الزبن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كلا rebukes the forbidding person again; the Prophet must persist in obedience, continue prostrating, and draw near to God.
rows.anchor: ردع أيضا للناهي. { لا تطعه } أي أثبت أنت على طاعتك

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A Prophetic report says a servant is nearest his Lord while prostrating.
rows.anchor: أقرب ما يكون العبد إلى ربه إذا سجد

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report promises the reciter a reward as though he had recited the entire set of shorter suras.
rows.anchor: من قرأ سورة العلق أعطي من الأجر كأنما قرأ المفصل كله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun refers to the Qur'an, magnifying it by leaving it unmentioned and by attributing its sending-down to God; the night itself is magnified by the rhetorical question and answer.
rows.anchor: الضمير للقرآن فخمه بإضماره من غير ذكر شهادة له بالنباهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its descent on the Night of Decree may mean revelation began that night or that the whole Qur'an was sent from the Preserved Tablet to the lowest heaven, then Gabriel revealed it piecemeal over twenty-three years.
rows.anchor: وإنزاله فيها بأن ابتدأ بإنزاله فيها، أو أنزله جملة من اللوح إلى السماء الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation says the Qur'an was sent down concerning the night and its virtue; the night falls among the last ten odd nights of Ramadan, perhaps the seventh.
rows.anchor: وقيل المعنى { أنزلنه } في فضلها وهي في أوتار العشر الأخير في رمضان،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The night is concealed so a seeker will enliven many nights; its name indicates either honor or the decree of affairs, as 44:4 states.
rows.anchor: والداعي إلى إخفائها أن يحيي من يريدها ليالي كثيرة، وتسميتها بذلك لشرفها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The thousand months may be an expression for a very long time, or may refer to a report about an Israelite who fought armed in God's way for a thousand months, prompting believers to marvel at their lesser deeds.
rows.anchor: أو لما روي أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام ذكر إسرائيليا يلبس السلاح في سبيل الله ألف شهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Angels and the Spirit descend either to earth, to the lowest heaven, or near to the believers; they descend because of every decree of the year, though a reading makes it “for every person.”
rows.anchor: بيان لما له فصلت على ألف شهر وتنزلهم إلى الأرض، أو إلى السماء الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The night is entirely safety, with only safety decreed on it unlike nights that bring both safety and trial; alternatively, it is called peace because angels frequently greet believers.
rows.anchor: ما هي إلا سلامة أي لا يقدر الله فيها إلا السلامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The night lasts until dawn; al-Kisāʾī reads the word with kasra as a time noun by analogy or irregularly.
rows.anchor: أي وقت مطلعه أي طلوعه. وقرأ الكسائي بالكسر

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report promises the reward of fasting Ramadan and keeping the Night of Decree in worship to whoever recites the sura.
